descriptionChirho: Physical turning of the body or changing direction; Arabic الْتَفَتَ (iltafata, turn around) consistently across all persons/numbers; Korean 돌아보았다/돌이켰다/돌았다 (turned/turned back); Swahili -geuka (turn); includes consecutive imperfects, perfects, imperfects, imperatives, jussives, and infinitives expressing the basic Qal sense of turning or changing direction

Static orientation or direction that something faces, not active turning; Arabic مُتَّجِهَة/مُتَوَجِّهَة (muttajiha, directed/facing) and يَتَّجِهُ (yattajihu, is directed); Korean 향하는 (hyanghanun, facing toward); Swahili -elekea (head toward/face); predominantly participles and imperfects describing the orientation of gates, buildings, or directions

Turning one's attention or gaze toward someone, often implying regard or consideration; Hindi देखा (dekha, saw) and ध्यान दिया (gave attention); Swahili -angalia (look at); Arabic الْتَفَتَ in context of looking at someone with attention; Korean 돌아보셨도다 (turned and looked, with honorific implying divine regard)

Temporal or figurative turning away, declining, or passing; Arabic فَنَتْ (fanat, perished/vanished) and مَالَ (mala, inclined/declined) — different roots from core الْتَفَتَ indicating genuine polysemy; Korean 지나갔다 (passed away) and 기울었다 (inclined/declined); Swahili -pita (pass); Spanish declinar/declinaron

Temporal use of the infinitive construct with preposition, meaning 'at the turn of' (evening, morning); Arabic عِنْدَ إِقْبَالِ (at the approach of) and عِنْدَ الْتِفَاتِ (at the turning of); Spanish al amanecer (at dawn), al volverse; Swahili wakati wa (time of), kabla ya (before); used in temporal expressions for transitions of the day

Intensive/causative Piel stem meaning to clear, prepare, or make ready (especially a road or space); Arabic هَيِّئُوا (prepare!) and افْسَحُوا (make room!); Korean 예비하라 (prepare!); Swahili -tayarisha (prepare); Spanish preparad; semantically distinct from Qal turning — this is about clearing obstacles or preparing a path

Intensive/causative Piel stem meaning to turn something away or remove it; Arabic أَبْعَدَ (ab'ada, remove/distance); Korean 쫓아내셨다 (drove out); Swahili ameufagilia (swept away); Hindi फेर दिया (turned away); semantically distinct from preparing — this is active removal or turning away of something

Piel stem used for emptying or evacuating; Arabic يُفْرِغُونَ (yufrighuna, they pour out/empty); Korean 비우리라 (will empty); Swahili wataifanya tupu (will make empty); Spanish vaciarán (will empty); a distinct Piel sense of making vacant

Causative Hifil stem meaning to cause someone or something to turn, or to turn something oneself; Arabic أَدَارُوا (adaruu, they turned/rotated something); Korean 돌렸다 (dollyo-da, caused to turn); Swahili -geuza (cause to turn, transitive); Hindi फेर लिया/मोड़ा (turned something); distinct from intransitive Qal turning

Nominal/substantival use meaning a corner or angle of a structure; Arabic الزَّاوِيَةِ (az-zawiya, the corner); Korean 모퉁이 (corner); Swahili Kona (corner); Spanish la Esquina (the corner); Hindi कोने (corners); entirely different semantic domain from verbal senses
